extracted.intended_audience: readers/students of art history; artists and architects interested in medieval/early Renaissance Italian practice
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria for judging and producing medieval Italian sculpture, mosaic, painting, and architecture — emphasizing design, technique, proportion, material durability, narrative composition, and workshop practice. Useful for historians, restorers, or practitioners seeking period-relevant quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and correct proportions
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should be 'designed and executed perfectly in all its parts and with all its proportions.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good architecture is judged by coherent overall design and correct proportions (e.g., use of columns, architraves, measured sections). Anti-pattern: grand expense or ornament without sound proportional design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical execution and diligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures and ornamentation should be produced with 'infinite patience and diligence' and careful workmanship even if design is imperfect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patience in carving/detailing is a mark of quality (Niccola's pulpit figures). Scoring note: finish and attentive carving raise otherwise imperfect designs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Durability and solidity of construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Works should be solid and long-lasting — mosaic pieces 'very well put together' and architecture built so parts 'support the whole mass' of vaulting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for methods and materials that ensure longevity (mosaic, robust foundations). Anti-pattern: pretty but fragile execution or badly founded structures that 'threaten to fall down.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothness and precision in mosaic work
rubrics_metrics.description: Mosaic should be 'smooth as a table' with pieces 'very well put together' and cemented diligently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical neatness—tight tesserae placement and smooth surface—are central; rough, uneven mosaics are judged inferior regardless of subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faithful use of classical orders and structural logic
rubrics_metrics.description: Good practice includes correct application of orders and measured assembly of columns and elements so that the building's parts function structurally and visually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Corinthian-order marbles and granite columns arranged to create properly proportioned architraves and vaults. Anti-pattern: arbitrary reworking that departs from sound ancient methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joinery and unity of many pieces
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerous pieces should be joined and cemented so well that 'the whole work is easily judged... to be all of one piece.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High craftsmanship in assembling multi-piece works (inlaid altars, multi-part façades) is praised; visible seams or poor joins reduce perceived quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expressive appropriateness to subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Imagery should match its theme — e.g., in representations of Paradise give 'the greatest beauty', while in Hell make 'the strangest forms of devils' intent on tormenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotional and formal choices must serve the narrative/theological intent. Scoring: coherence between expression and subject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalistic portraiture from life
rubrics_metrics.description: Portraits taken 'from nature' (i.e., life) are valued — e.g., portrait of Niccola carved from nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate likeness and observation of the sitter are marks of superior sculptural/painted portraiture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carving 'in the round' and mastery of relief depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Skill includes making figures 'almost wholly detached from the marble' (fully in the round) and competent half-/low-relief work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical mastery over depths of relief and three-dimensional modelling distinguishes better sculpture from rudimentary, flat carving.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative composition and orderly scene division
rubrics_metrics.description: Large works should be composed into clear narrative scenes (e.g., pulpit divided into five scenes from the life of Christ, mosaics arranged in friezes/circles depicting ordered cycles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear sequencing and distribution of episodes aid comprehension and aesthetic effect. Anti-pattern: cluttered or incoherent narrative arrangement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good counsel and expert planning before construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who 'put their hand to building' should 'take counsel... from the best' to avoid repented errors and structural failures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consultation with experienced masters/architects during planning prevents costly mistakes. Scoring: evidence of informed oversight and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design, invention, grace, and manner over mere expense
rubrics_metrics.description: Great cost, labour, or diligence must be accompanied by 'good design' and 'excellence of invention, grace, and manner' to be truly valuable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Money and effort alone do not guarantee quality; originality of concept, elegance of composition, and stylistic refinement are decisive. Anti-pattern: lavish but poorly designed monuments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrated use of mixed materials and fine detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective works may combine marble, mosaic, enamel, and bronze with 'much diligence' to produce delicate and harmonious effect (e.g., altar with enamels and mosaics let into marble).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful integration and fine detailing of multiple media raise the work's status; sloppy combination or incongruous materials detract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apprenticeship, workshop teaching, and transmission of skill
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful masters train apprentices who later spread techniques (e.g., Germans apprenticed to Giovanni who later worked in Rome and Orvieto); teaching is part of producing a school of good work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of a coherent workshop tradition, documented pupils, and transmission of methods is an indicator of mature practice and sustained quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-cultural learning and emulation as drivers of improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning from other traditions (e.g., Andrea learning mosaic from Greek painters in Venice; Germans working with Italians) and competition/emulation spur improvements in art and architecture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Openness to foreign techniques and healthy competition among craftsmen are positive; isolation or hostile refusal to adopt better methods retards progress.
